notes: The Volksblatt prints the first round's votes by municipality for the Oberland, with Schaan and Planken counted together, and only district totals for the Unterland. It leaves Ludwig Beck's votes in Balzers, Triesen and Triesenberg open ("?"), and prints Heinrich Brunhart's municipal votes adding up to 374 against his total of 373; both are stored as printed.
The second round's votes by municipality come from the same paper's report of the runoff. The substitutes (Ersatzmänner) elected on the same day are not stored.

The first round's table is a compilation from the municipalities' main vote lists (Zusammenstellung aus den Hauptstimmlisten) that the Volksblatt printed as a submitted article; the second round's votes come from the Oberrheinische Nachrichten's table of the runoff (Verteilung der Stimmen). Neither paper prints the valid ballots. A dash in the table is stored as 0 votes.

The government's notice (Kundmachung) lists only the elected candidates and those who went to the runoff. It prints Josef Gaßner's municipal votes adding up to 732 against a total of 782, Wilhelm Büchel's adding up to 385 against 384, and, for the runoff, Alois Frick's adding up to 606 against 676 (Triesen is printed 27); all are stored as printed.

The government's notice lists every candidate. Josef Marxer (Vorsteher, Eschen) is printed with municipal votes adding up to 326 against a total of 336; stored as printed. Three cells whose type does not tell 3 from 8 were read so that their row adds up to its printed total (Brunhart in Vaduz 123, Franz Hoop in Eschen 89 and Schellenberg 33).

The government's notice gives the revised count after the Volkspartei's complaint, with the first count in brackets; the revised count is stored. Three Oberland candidates tied on 689 votes for the runoff place and the lot sent Franz Amann and Alois Jehle to it. The Unterland table heads its last column Gamprin a second time; it is Ruggell. The runoff's protocol prints Balzers with 257 ballots against 148 valid, 8 invalid and 103 blank; stored as printed.

The government's notice of the supplementary election of four Oberland members, after the Volkspartei members had resigned. It prints Johann Schädler's municipal votes adding up to 700 against a total of 690; stored as printed.

From 1932 each municipality except Planken elected one member, and the remaining five (four for the Oberland, one for the Unterland) were elected by the whole country a week later. The government's notice of the municipal round prints, for each municipality, the electoral roll, the ballots, and only the elected candidate's votes, so the other candidates' votes are not stored. In the national round it prints Peter Büchel's municipal votes adding up to 1,260 against 1,262 and Rudolf Amann's to 868 against 869; stored as printed.

The municipal round's figures come from the table the Liechtensteiner Vaterland printed; in Eschen and Mauren the Union put up no candidate. The national round's figures come from the government's notice after the electoral commission's review; it prints no ballot counts.
